title: Gideon and the Choir
premise: Jude Yarrow, a former battle-priest turned charm-seller, discovers that the god he swore to—the Choir—did not die but was silenced by the usurper Vael Corrin, who stole its voice to power his armies. When the border wards collapse and the stars go out, Jude is the last living conduit of the old covenant, hunted by both the usurper's inquisitors and the desperate free cities that outlawed his kind. Guided by a defected choir-singer named Sera and a ghost-choir only he can hear, Jude journeys to the Silent Spire to reforge the covenant, learning it demands a voice freely given—not a life taken. In the climax he offers his own name and memory to wake the Choir, ending the usurper's stolen magic at the cost of forgetting who he was; Sera and the free cities give him a new belonging, teaching him himself again.
about_author: Isandro Brightwater is the pen name of a former cathedral chorister who left music for manuscripts and now writes fantasy steeped in liturgy, silence, and stubborn hope. They live near a cold coastline, where they claim the fog sings if you listen long enough.

chapters.title: Charms for a Godless City
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In the city of Ashfall, Jude sells hollow charms to superstitious buyers while hiding the faint warmth of his dead god's mark. A child buys a luck-knot that shouldn't work—and does. Emotional beat: quiet shame and longing, the ache of a man surviving on scraps of a faith he pretends is over.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The stars vanish one by one; the border wards shatter like glass; every charm in Ashfall flares alive. Inquisitors sweep the streets as Jude's brand burns white-hot, dragging him toward something calling his true name. Emotional beat: terror and terrible recognition—the silence breaking after fifteen years.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were Holding Back
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. A defected choir-singer crosses the fallen border, fleeing Vael Corrin's inquisitors, carrying a shard of the stolen Voice. She reaches Ashfall hunting rumors of a living conduit. Emotional beat: exhausted resolve; she has buried too many conduits to hope easily.

chapters.title: The Mark That Wouldn't Fade
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Interrogated by Ashfall's wardens, Jude hides his burning brand until Sera breaks into his cell, recognizing him as the last conduit of the Choir. She offers escape and answers he isn't sure he wants. Emotional beat: cornered defiance curdling into reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Small Lies
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, flashback-woven. Fleeing through the undercity, Jude recalls the covenant's breaking: the Choir falling silent mid-battle, his order slaughtered, his survival bought by desertion. Sera calls it what it was—a price, not a betrayal. Emotional beat: guilt confronted, not absolved.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Decide
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The pair reach Meridian, where a council of free cities debates surrendering conduits to Corrin rather than face his armies. Jude is displayed like evidence. An old general, once his comrade, casts the deciding vote to shelter him. Emotional beat: humiliation sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: Lessons in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Training in Meridian's hidden archive, Jude relearns the covenant rites from a half-mad archivist while the ghost-choir hums fragments only he hears. His first working spell in fifteen years nearly kills him. Emotional beat: clumsy joy shadowed by fear of what mastery will cost.

chapters.title: Corrin's Beautiful Machine
chapters.summary: Vael Corrin's POV. The usurper conducts his stolen Voice like an orchestra, forging soldiers whose fear is literally sung away. He learns a conduit lives and sends his Hand, Inquisitor Maren, once Sera's mentor. Emotional beat: chilling serenity; Corrin believes he saved the world from gods.

chapters.title: The Road Through Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The company travels toward the Silent Spire through a village emptied by Corrin's song-taken soldiers—people alive but vacant, humming. Jude recognizes the tune: it's from the Choir. Emotional beat: horror and heartbreak; the enemy is using his god's own music.

chapters.title: Maren's Offer
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Maren corners them, offering amnesty if Sera returns and the conduit surrenders. Sera refuses, and their duel reveals Maren is partially song-taken herself, fighting her own conditioning. Emotional beat: grief between people who loved each other before ideology broke them.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Wounded and doubting, Jude learns the covenant's full terms from the ghost-choir: it requires a voice given freely, permanently—one's name, memory, self. He tells no one. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in grim acceptance; he's already survived one price.

chapters.title: The Council Fractures
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. News of Corrin's approaching army splits the free cities; two sign secret terms. The general who saved Jude is assassinated by song-taken agents inside Meridian. Emotional beat: despair; the alliance built on hope begins eating itself.

chapters.title: A Name Sung Back
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In the archives' deepest vault, the ghost-choir coalesces enough to speak: they are the dead conduits, and they chose silence fifteen years ago to keep the Voice from being fully stolen. Jude rages at their cowardice. Emotional beat: fury at the dead, and the first crack of understanding.

chapters.title: The Battle of the Salt Gate
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Corrin's vanguard hits Meridian. Jude, untrained in war-magic, holds the gate by singing the covenant raw, saving hundreds and revealing himself to every spy in the city. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into exposure—he has become a target no wall can hide.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Maren captures Sera during the retreat, and Corrin uses her knowledge to locate the Silent Spire. Tortured with her own stolen memories played back as song, Sera resists—but breaks just enough. Emotional beat: endurance at its absolute limit.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Confession
chapters.summary: Vael Corrin's POV. Alone with the Voice, Corrin admits what he buried: the Choir went silent because it begged him to stop feeding it war, and he answered by cutting out its tongue. Emotional beat: self-deception cracking; the villain knows exactly what he is.

chapters.title: The March to the Silent Spire
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. With Meridian fallen, Jude leads survivors on a winter march to the Spire, pursued by Corrin's main host. The ghost-choir grows louder, hungrier, testing whether he'll still pay the price. Emotional beat: weary determination; a pilgrimage disguised as a retreat.

chapters.title: Maren Chooses
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Guarding captive Sera at the Spire's foot, Maren hears the ghost-choir singing a lullaby from her childhood—proof the god remembers even the traitors. She frees Sera and turns on Corrin's column, dying to buy an hour. Emotional beat: redemption purchased at the last possible moment.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At the Spire's heart, Jude begins the covenant rite as Corrin arrives, the two conduits of the same broken god facing each other across the altar. Jude speaks his renunciation: his name, his memories, his self, freely given. Emotional beat: transcendent terror; the sacrifice made without hesitation.

chapters.title: Every Voice at Once
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The Choir wakes through Jude and every freed song-taken soul; the stars reignite; Corrin's stolen Voice tears out of him, leaving an ordinary, hollowed man. The dead conduits welcome Jude home—and then, gently, let him go. Emotional beat: catharsis; the whole book's tension released in light and sound.

chapters.title: The Man Who Forgot Himself
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Jude survives, alive but blank—no name, no past, no guilt. Sera refuses to let the covenant take everything: she begins telling him who he was, story by story, choosing which truths to return. Emotional beat: tender grief; identity rebuilt as a gift rather than a burden.

chapters.title: Gideon and the Choir
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Months later, in a free city where magic is law again, a man called Gideon teaches children the old songs, remembering almost nothing but feeling all of it. When the Choir hums, he hums back. Emotional beat: belonging earned at last—not restored, but newly made.
